02 / THE MECHANICS

ONE UPDATE.
THREE MOMENTS.

You change the DOM.
The browser connects the dots.

01

CAPTURE THE BEFORE.

The browser captures the current view. Give an element a unique view-transition-name to track it separately.

OLD STATE → SNAPSHOT
02{↗}

MAKE YOUR CHANGE.

Update the DOM inside the callback. Move a card, reorder a list, or replace content. Keep the update small and predictable.

startViewTransition(update)
03

CONNECT THE STATES.

The browser animates the snapshots. Shape the timing and motion with CSS pseudo-elements, then let the overlay disappear.

::view-transition-group(name)

The lifecycle above describes same-document transitions. Cross-document transitions use navigation and CSS opt-in. Explore the full lifecycle on MDN ↗

03 / TAKE IT INTO THE FIELD

MOTION WITH
A PURPOSE.

A transition should explain a change.
Build the interaction first. Add motion second.

PROGRESSIVE
ENHANCEMENT
BY DESIGN ↗
01 Always ship the fallback. +

Feature-detect document.startViewTransition and run the same update directly when unavailable. A skipped animation must never prevent a state change. Cross-document support is separate; regular links still navigate.

02 Motion is a preference. +

Check prefers-reduced-motion: reduce in JavaScript and CSS. Apply the state update without the transition. Let people reduce motion further, and respond if the system preference changes.

03 Keep identity stable. +

Use a unique name for each rendered element in a snapshot. Match the same logical object across states, never its array position. Duplicate names can skip the animation. The newer match-element value follows element identity within one document; check its support separately.

04 Focus is part of the transition. +

Preserve focus when an existing control stays on screen. If a view replaces the focused element, intentionally move focus to the new content and restore it when going back. Use semantic buttons and concise live announcements for updates that would otherwise be missed.

05 Keep the browser’s job small. +

Fetch data and decode images before starting a transition. Await your framework’s DOM commit inside the update callback. Avoid too many individually named elements, and use browser developer tools to inspect the snapshot animation.
